experience.title: Founder and Platform Engineer
experience.org: AetherGrid  |  Open-source AI workload orchestrator  |  Nairobi
bullets: Designed and built AetherGrid end to end with Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL (raw psycopg, no ORM), React, TypeScript, Docker Compose and GitHub Actions. Four layers with a domain core that has no infrastructure imports. {{tests}} passing tests across unit, contract, integration, API and end-to-end, and {{adrs}} ADRs.

Built a multi-dimensional best-fit scheduler across CPU, memory and VRAM, with time-bound leases renewed for the full run of a job. Reconciliation reclaims work from dead workers, expired leases, offline nodes and jobs abandoned mid-cancellation, within a bounded retry budget.

Found and closed a recurring race-condition class by fencing lease release, outcome reporting and renewal on lease identity, then fencing reconciliation's own deletes by expiry. Each fix began with a test that reproduced the bug and was verified against real PostgreSQL.

Built a real subprocess engine with enforced timeouts and two-stage termination (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), with cancellation delivered over the lease-renewal channel and an explicit CANCELLING state. Built a standalone worker agent with capped exponential backoff and full jitter that re-registers after control plane restarts, one API key per agent.

Kept the API responsive during database outages by moving reconciliation off the event loop, splitting liveness from readiness and bounding the pool timeout to 5 seconds. Worst-case latency on an unrelated endpoint dropped from about 29 s to 0.124 s, measured against a stopped Postgres container.

Secured the API with key authentication on every route, scoped keys (jobs:execute, keys:manage), key ownership and locally minted first keys. Hardened containers: non-root, read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, pinned digests, database password as a Docker secret. A CI workflow asserts each property, and each check was proven to fail on a deliberate break.

Implemented tenant scoping for API keys, nodes and jobs. The tenant comes from the credential, never the request, and another tenant's resource answers like a missing one. Workers, leases and events are the next stage.

Built a resilient HTTP client (retries, circuit breaker, OAuth2, mTLS, replay of only safe requests) and a React 19 operator dashboard with a live event feed, per-job history and a Playwright end-to-end test in CI.
